_comment: Copy to ~/.config/hongyan/config.json and edit. This file is CONFIG only: logs, queue and message history live in ~/.local/state/hongyan, the socket and pids in $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/hongyan, the speech-to-text model in ~/.local/share/hongyan — so this directory can be copied or backed up without carrying your conversations along. All four roots honour their XDG_* variables. The ACI is the ONLY authentication — Signal validates it cryptographically. Phone numbers are display attributes and are never used to authorize.
_transport_note: bot_account (default, recommended) = hongyan has its own Signal account and a second phone number, and can only ever see messages addressed to it. note_to_self = hongyan is a LINKED DEVICE on YOUR account and answers in Note to Self, so no second number is needed — but a linked device receives a copy of every conversation you have, and anyone who compromises this server gets your whole Signal account, not a throwaway bot. Read the README before choosing it.
_freshness_note: Messages older than this are answered with a notice instead of acted on, so a backlog cannot replay after downtime.
_throttle_note: Burst cooldown, not an hourly cap. A cap punishes normal conversation and fails silently; a cooldown only reacts to a genuine flood, always announces itself, and clears on its own.
_model_note: Nous Research (https://portal.nousresearch.com) — an OpenAI-compatible endpoint serving several free models, with a documented public API and no client restriction. Get a key, put it in key_file (mode 600). OpenCode Zen was the original default and is NOT usable here any more: its free tier refuses any request without an x-opencode-session header ('OpenCode's free tier can only be used in OpenCode'), and a Zen API key does not lift that — the restriction is on the free models, not on the absence of a key.
_providers_note: A chain entry is 'model' (default_provider) or 'provider:model'; the split is on the first colon, so Nous ids keep theirs ('nous:inclusionai/ling-3.0-flash-fin:free'). Nous REJECTS an untagged request outright, and wants the tags in the request body — sent as a header they are ignored and the refusal reads as the model declining rather than the request being malformed. A 'user=' tag is required specifically. The tags are product attribution and name nobody.
_chain_note: Ordered fallbacks; the first channel that answers wins. Verified free on 2026-09-08, all seven honouring a strict JSON-only prompt. Text runs biggest-context first: LongCat 2.0 (1M) -> Solar Pro 4 (524K) -> the two Ling 3.0 Flash variants -> Laguna S. Vision needs an image-capable model: Step 3.7 Flash is the only free one here. A channel failing with gone/credit-wall errors is benched until YOU look at it — you get an alert and a queue action item, the fallback answers meanwhile, and 'use <model>' puts it back. Temporary failures (overload, timeouts) only earn a two-minute cooldown. Keep more than two entries: a chain that heals down to one has no fallback left, and one misbehaving model becomes every reply.
_timeout_note: Generous on purpose. A typing indicator runs while the model works, so a slow answer looks like thinking rather than a hang. Short timeouts silently queued real questions. Never set a max_tokens: reasoning models emit reasoning before content, and any cap risks an empty reply.
_steps_note: Agent loop budget. The model chooses read-only steps (search / open a page / server probe / weather) until it can answer. Bounded because each step costs a round trip, and because a query composed after reading fetched text is a channel injected content could try to steer.
_stt_note: Voice notes: command transcribes one audio file to stdout, path appended as the last argument. hongyan-stt wraps ffmpeg + whisper.cpp (see the script header for one-time setup); everything spawns per note and exits, so idle RAM cost is zero. Leave command empty to keep voice notes disabled.
_adaptive_reasoning_note: The router already judges every message in the call it was making anyway; with this on, its low/high verdict also sets reasoning_effort on the wire — trivial questions think in zero tokens, hard ones get real reasoning. Unknown verdicts leave the model's own default. Off = no automatic adjustment; asking in so many words ('think hard', 'just answer') is always honoured regardless.
_monthly_review_note: Who runs the monthly review. 'local' = this machine does it itself (one-device setup). 'remote' = a second machine with a full agent owns it, so this one stays quiet rather than sending a second, contradictory report. 'off' = no review. Either way nothing is sent on a schedule: when the review comes due it is offered after your next message and delivered only if you reply yes — or type 'do the monthly review' to run it on demand.
_roster_check_note: Off by default. When true, the monthly review asks the provider for its current model roster. That is an unattended request to a service this program is only a client of, and some providers' terms restrict programmatic clients they did not publish — so it is opt-in. With it off, nothing contacts the provider except to answer a message you sent, and a model that disappears reports itself the next time it is needed.
_site_note: How the assistant describes the machine it lives on, and where its home-directory probes look.
_services_note: How to check each service. type: user | system | port. Getting this wrong reports healthy services as dead — a user service checked as a system service always looks inactive, and anything in a container may have no service entry at all, only a listening port. unit defaults to the service name.
_allowed_units_note: Restartable units. Keep to user units unless the account has passwordless sudo — listing units it cannot touch only produces confusing failures.
_allowed_jobs_note: Named commands the owner may re-run by typing 'rerun <name>'. Never reachable from free text or from a model.
_custom_commands_note: Extra read-only commands for this host, typed exactly or reached by a synonym. show_unit pairs the output with a service state check.
_custom_probes_note: Extra probes the agent may name while answering. Same safety boundary as the built-ins: the model emits a NAME and the code decides what it runs, so a name that is not defined here is dropped.
_http_probes_note: Any JSON API becomes a probe: name -> {url, key or key_file, key_header, path (dot path, [*] collects), desc}. The model picks the NAME; the URL and key stay in config.
_media_apps_note: qbittorrent: {url, user, pass or pass_file} -> downloads command. overseerr: {url, key or key_file} -> requests command. sonarr/radarr: {url, key or key_file} -> releases command.
_webhook_note: If webhook_port is set, the listener listens on 127.0.0.1:<port> for POST /sonarr|/radarr|/plex — point the apps webhooks at it and events arrive as Signal messages. webhook_token (optional) is checked as ?token= or X-Hongyan-Token.
_socket_note: The daemon socket is derived, not configured: $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/hongyan/socket, falling back to ~/.local/state/hongyan/run/socket where there is no runtime dir. Set "socket" here only if you need a specific path — pinning /run/user/<uid> in a config file is what breaks it on the next machine.
